findings.issue: contradicts task clause: clause 1 says each cell asserts 'the filter bar and the count are each one line', and R18's resolution (which clause 2 implements) asks for 'a single-line bar at rest, filtered and in every view'. lm4 instead asserts `at.barLines <= at.barNeeds` - the bar may take as many lines as its controls need packed end to end - and its own comment says the 1512x945 bar still takes a second line once anything filters on acme, demo-large and the live plan (92px against 60px at rest, per the executor's measurement). The count is one line (lm3); the bar is not, and the check written for it was relaxed to pass.
findings.resolution: Take the design decision the executor named (the count out of the pinned bar's flow - e.g. its own line under the bar that scrolls, or into the strip - or expand/Clear out of the bar), then make lm4 assert barLines === 1 at the laptop sizes (and say where a phone is exempt and why), so the matrix holds the clause rather than describing the shortfall.

findings.issue: `#audit-count{flex:0 0 auto;white-space:nowrap}` removes the count's only way to fit a line narrower than its text. Judged from reading, not run: on this repo's plan filtered the count reads like '6 of 166 phases · 4 of 1543 tasks, 3 cancelled not counted' - the executor measured it at 391px at 1512 (15px), so about 378px at the phone's 14.5px - while the bar's content box at 390px wide is roughly 342px (body padding .75rem each side plus the bar's .75rem padding). Unbreakable and unshrinkable, it overflows the bar's card sideways (and may give the page a horizontal scroll). No matrix question can see it: lm3 counts lines (one), and lm4's packer starts a new line for a control wider than the room, so a too-wide count raises `barNeeds` and passes.
findings.resolution: Add a per-cell matrix question that every in-flow control of .sectools, and the count's drawn rects, lie inside the bar's content box and that document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth; prove it red on the live render at 390x844 with a chip on. Then let the count wrap where the bar is a phone's width (e.g. white-space:normal under max-width:40rem, where the bar is not the laptop's one-line problem), or shorten the filtered clause.

findings.issue: lm1's allowed layers are whatever is computed `position:sticky` over the scan column, the top bar included. So lm1 cannot see the top bar pinning where the forced-colors.css rule says it must scroll (max-width:52rem or max-height:32rem): the bound grows with it. The executor's own mutation 'top bar sticky on phones' went red only on lm2 (520px against the 422px ceiling), not lm1. The ph1 it replaced held the phone stacks to the strip and the shut filter bar explicitly, so it caught any top-bar pinning, not only one large enough to cross half the screen. The forced-colors.css comment still names lm1 as what measures this rule.
findings.resolution: In stackInTable, read matchMedia('(max-width:52rem),(max-height:32rem)') and, where it matches, drop the top bar from the allowed layers (fail lm1 if it is sticky there), keeping the computed-sticky derivation for wider and taller cells. Re-run the 'top bar sticky on phones' mutation and confirm lm1 itself goes red.

findings.issue: Clause 1 requires the gate to run on a fixture carrying the Sort select. The chosen fixture is the live render in verify.sh's rendered_plan_legs, which carries #audit-sort only while _report_html.any_phase_pinned() is true for this plan (it is today). Nothing in the matrix or the leg asserts or notes that #audit-sort was present, so the day no phase is pinned the Sort-select coverage disappears with every cell still green.
findings.resolution: Have the matrix note per run whether #audit-sort was drawn, and either make the live leg fail when it is absent or add a committed fixture with a pinned phase to the gate's fixture list.
